stem.text: $1.0\,\text{mol}$ of an organic compound, J, requires $6.0\,\text{mol}$ of oxygen for complete combustion.
$1.0\,\text{mol}$ of J reacts with sodium, producing $0.50\,\text{mol}$ of a gas that gives a ‘pop’ with a lighted splint.
J reacts with an excess of hot acidified potassium manganate(VII) to produce an organic compound which gives an orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNPH reagent.
